$comment: Bundle budget for the built web client, checked by scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs after vite build (CI web job). Sizes are bytes; gzip is zlib level 6, as in the vite build report. Raise a limit only with a reason in the PR. See ptone/scion#5306.

manualChunks.$comment: Packages vite.config.ts places in a named chunk; forbiddenModules rules refer to them with chunkPackages, so the list lives in one place. Only packages no other code uses may be listed (isolatedChunks checks the result).

chunks.$comment: CodeMirror editor core (ptone/scion#5351). Each language is its own lazily loaded lang-<name> chunk (vite.config.ts), so this chunk holds only the core: @codemirror/view, state, language, autocomplete, commands, search and @lezer/common, highlight (409,273 B raw at the split, from 783,936 B with every language). The design's 350,000 B estimate assumed about 430 KB of languages; they measured about 350 KB, so the limit was revised to 420,000 B with webperf-lead approval.
chunks.$comment-review-editor: The graphical review editor (ptone/scion#5913): Milkdown, ProseMirror and the remark stack plus the editor modules, loaded only when a review opens in the graphical view. combined: the limit is for all review-editor-* chunks together (the packages chunk and the editor modules' chunk). Measured at 142,409 B gzip / 454,689 B raw after leaving out the Markdown presets' commands, keymaps and input rules (ptone/scion#5914; from 159,881 B gzip / 514,668 B raw); the limit is that plus 20 kB gzip and 70 kB raw for the later editor work. Raise it only with measured numbers.

$comment-isolatedChunks: The review editor chunks (ptone/scion#5913) are reached only through import(): no other chunk, lazy ones included, may import them statically (a shared package placed in them would make, for example, the CodeMirror chunk download the whole editor).

chunkImports.$comment: The review editor chunks (ptone/scion#5913) may import statically only each other, the small shared chunks made for them (key names, CommonJS helpers) and what the artifact page has already loaded (the entry, Lit, Shoelace, the preview frame and the Markdown renderer).

$comment-requiredStrings: Marker strings of the review editor's safety and input modules (ptone/scion#5914), each a literal that occurs in exactly one source file, its module (artifact-review/bundle-markers.test.ts checks this): safe-render.ts's schema renderers (the Symbol that tags every renderer it replaces, raw HTML's included), its image placeholder and its link renderer; the paste plugin; the suggest-mode policy; the tracking plugin. The build drops plugin code nothing uses, so this proves these modules are in the production chunks, which the unit tests (run on the source) cannot.

forbiddenModules.$comment: The terminal workspace loads lazily (client/terminal-workspace-loader.ts). No terminal-* module may be in what the entry, the login route or the home route load statically. main.ts is listed itself so the entry is checked even if a route chunk stops importing it.

allow.reason: The lazy loader itself (a single-flight import() of the workspace chunk, no workspace code); main.ts must reach it statically.
Event-name and drag-MIME constants only (no workspace code); the header imports TERMINAL_SESSION_COUNT_EVENT on every route.

forbiddenModules.$comment: The graphical review editor (ptone/scion#5913) loads lazily through review-editor-loader.ts. None of its modules, nor Milkdown, ProseMirror or the remark stack, may be in what the entry, the login and home routes or the artifact page load statically, so plain artifact viewing never downloads it.

allow.reason: The lazy loader itself (a single-flight import of the editor chunk, no editor code); the artifact page must reach it statically.
